we stood a cage back up, but then it started raining again. gonna have to put some stakes in the cages to stop them from falling. Grr.

On a lighter note, have been harvesting a little. I got the upright freezer i mentioned in my last update, and we have lots of space for the veggies now :)

Pulled most of the turnips and greens, cooked them, and froze them. The rest of the greens are bad, but i will still pull the turnips and cook them by themselves for freezing.

we have been eating lots of yellow squash and zukes, and the other day we blanched and froze like 5 yellow, and 2 or 3 zukes.

Cukes are coming in; we have a bowl of sliced cukes on kitchen table now. Feels like summer :)

I have harvested abou 20 jalapenos, and frozen them. My fav to do is ABT (atomic buffalo turds, the first G**gle recipe is the one we use).

Harvested probably 5 hot banana peppers so far (or apparently, hungarian wax peppers). There is a recipe on allrecipes for stuffed banana peppers, and it is AWESOME. Had never tried stuffed peppers aside from bell before.

Tomatoes are coming in, but still green. Im dealing with blossom-end rot right now, and losing :( But i can fry up some green ones before the rot gets them. I have now been told by a couple people to put lime on them as the only remedy. Have done the "spray" and it hasnt remedied the issue. Will try pulverized lime next.

SBVs are whats killing my squash and zukes. i actually pulled a dead plant the other day, and saw the worm inside the stalk. I was reading that if you plant after July, its past their egg-laying cycle, so i will continually replant for a while. I have probably 5-10 new plants that are very small at the moment, and will replace the dead ones with new seeds in the next few days.

Potato plants are not looking happy. bottom leaves are browning and dying :( I only lightly fertilised them with nitrogen, so im thinking they MAY need a little more. Hell, i think the entire garden needs more, but EVERY DAMN TIME i want to fertilise, its either raining or gonna rain. I use blood meal and fish fertiliser. The fish is faster-acting, but it must be mixed with water and diluted. Im afraid i might drown my plants.

Thats about it for now, but will do pic update in a few days. work schedule is fucky.

Happy growing!

Everyone that enjoys reading fiction or watching science fiction movies/comics needs to read the first book on the Dune series by Frank Herbert. It's been called "the highest achievement of imagination", which I do not take lightly and wholeheartedly agree!

EDIT: the first book is just called Dune, by the way.

Just stay away, very far away from the movie adaptation by David Lynch. Don't even! The mini-series is much better but it covers later books in the series.
Could you elaborate on the writing of this book? A major problem I have with books is the way the author describes things (or fails to), is the book truly smooth and easy to read and comprehend?

It is by far the best book I've ever read and I don't know how much more I could say - I have read Dante's Inferno, the Odyssey, Lord of the Rings, Orwell, Huxley... I'm not sure Dune is the smoothest or most well-described book but it surely evokes beautiful images, landscapes (that have been reinterpreted countless times) - and most of all the ideas and plot.

This page lets you preview a sample of the book. Again, I strongly recommend it. https://books.google.com.br/books?id=p1MULH7JsTQC&source=gbs_book_other_versions

If you're a super fanatic about well-written books I have another suggestion for you but it doesn't really compare at all to Dune, it's just another very well written book (in style, the plot is very secondary there for me).
